# std.stream

<!-- Generated by `lang doc std` from the checked interfaces (lang 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Suspending input streams (e.g. from channels). Unlike `Seq`, pulling from
a stream may wait, and a stream is consumed as it is read: a `for` loop
that stops early leaves the rest readable. Closing a stream (`close`, or
an operation that stops at an error) closes what it reads from, so a
producer learns to stop.

## Types

### `Stream`

```lang
struct Stream<T, Eff> { pub next: fn() -> Option<T>, pub close: fn() -> Unit }
```

`Eff` is what pulling may do (and whether the stream captures task-local
state).

#### `Stream.batches`

```lang
fn batches(self: &Self, size: Int) -> Stream<List<T>, Eff>
```

#### `Stream.collect_at_most`

```lang
fn collect_at_most(self: &Self, limit: Int) -> Option<List<T>>
```

#### `Stream.drain`

```lang
fn drain(self: &Self) -> Int
```

#### `Stream.each`

```lang
fn each(self: &Self, f: fn(T) -> Unit !Eff) -> Unit
```

#### `Stream.filter`

```lang
fn filter(self: &Self, keep: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Stream<T, Eff>
```

#### `Stream.fold`

```lang
fn fold<A>(self: &Self, initial: A, f: fn(A, T) -> A !Eff) -> A
```

#### `Stream.map`

```lang
fn map<U>(self: &Self, f: fn(T) -> U !Eff) -> Stream<U, Eff>
```

```lang

```

```lang

```

#### `Stream.try_map`

```lang
fn try_map<U, E>(self: &Self, f: fn(T) -> Result<U, E> !Eff) -> Stream<Result<U, E>, Eff>
```

## Functions

### `batches`

```lang
fn batches<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, size: Int) -> Stream<List<T>, Eff>
```

Items in lists of `size` (the last may be shorter).

### `close`

```lang
fn close<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>) -> Unit
```

Stop reading `s` and release its source.

### `collect`

```lang
fn collect<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>) -> List<T> !{Wait, Eff}
```

Read every remaining item. This is unbounded: a stream that never ends
never returns, and a long one is held in memory whole (`collect_at_most`
bounds it).

### `collect_at_most`

```lang
fn collect_at_most<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, limit: Int) -> Option<List<T>>
```

Every remaining item when there are at most `limit`; otherwise
`none`, with the stream closed after reading one item past the limit.

### `drain`

```lang
fn drain<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>) -> Int
```

Read and discard every remaining item: how many there were.

### `each`

```lang
fn each<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, f: fn(T) -> Unit !Eff) -> Unit
```

Run `f` on each item.

### `filter`

```lang
fn filter<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, keep: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Stream<T, Eff>
```

### `fold`

```lang
fn fold<T, A, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, initial: A, f: fn(A, T) -> A !Eff) -> A
```

### `from_fn`

```lang
fn from_fn<T, Eff>(next: fn() -> Option<T> !Eff) -> Stream<T, Eff>
```

A stream pulling from `next`, with nothing to release.

### `from_list`

```lang
fn from_list<T>(items: List<T>) -> Stream<T, !{State}>
```

The items of a list, in order.

### `from_receiver`

```lang
fn from_receiver<T>(r: channel.Receiver<T>) -> Stream<T, !{Wait}>
```

Messages from a receiver until it is closed and drained. Closing the
stream closes the receiver: further sends fail.

### `map`

```lang
fn map<T, U, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, f: fn(T) -> U !Eff) -> Stream<U, Eff>
```

### `take`

```lang
fn take<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, n: Int) -> Stream<T, !{State, Eff}>
```

At most `n` items; the rest of `s` stays readable.

### `take_while`

```lang
fn take_while<T, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, keep: fn(T) -> Bool !Eff) -> Stream<T, !{State, Eff}>
```

Items while `keep` holds (the first that fails is consumed).

### `try_collect`

```lang
fn try_collect<T, E, Eff>(s: Stream<Result<T, E>, Eff>) -> Result<List<T>, E>
```

The items of a stream of results, or the first error (the stream is
then closed).

### `try_each`

```lang
fn try_each<T, E, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, f: fn(T) -> Result<Unit, E> !Eff) -> Result<Unit, E>
```

Run `f` on each item, stopping at the first error: the stream is
closed, and the error returned.

### `try_map`

```lang
fn try_map<T, U, E, Eff>(s: Stream<T, Eff>, f: fn(T) -> Result<U, E> !Eff) -> Stream<Result<U, E>, Eff>
```

A fallible transform: each item becomes `ok` or `err` (reading goes on;
`try_collect` and `try_each` stop at the first error).
